title: Early English Bibles render David 'brown'

points: At 1 Samuel 16:12 the King James reads that David was 'ruddy', and they say it means red; but the Matthew's Bible of 1537 reads 'he was brown with goodly eyes', and before it Coverdale had 'well coloured'. Ruddy in the English of that time meant brown: David was a black man.

source.title: OUR HIDDEN HISTORY | BIBLE CONSPIRACIES : REVISED VERSIONS EP 197

points: Tyndale (read as 1531) has 'ruddy'; the 1535 Coverdale Bible has 'well coloured'; the 1537 Matthew Bible 'brown with goodly eyes'; the 1539 Great Bible 'browned and of an excellent beauty'. Ruddy meant a healthy brown complexion; it was made to mean red later.

title: The Leo Frank case and Jim Conley
summary: Mary Phagan, 13, was murdered at the National Pencil Company in Atlanta in April 1913; the superintendent Leo Frank was convicted and in August 1915 lynched; the defence accused the black janitor Jim Conley.
account: Mary Phagan was strangled on April 26, 1913, at the National Pencil Company in Atlanta, where Leo Frank was superintendent. Police arrested several men, including Frank and Jim Conley, a janitor. Frank was convicted; on August 16, 1915, he was kidnapped from prison and lynched the next morning at Marietta.

Many African Americans opposed what historian Nancy MacLean called a 'virulently racist' characterization of Jim Conley, who was black, by the Frank defence. The case spurred the creation of the Anti-Defamation League and the resurgence of the Ku Klux Klan. In 1986 Georgia issued a pardon recognizing the state's failures, taking no stance on guilt; Wikipedia calls Frank wrongly convicted.

points: Leo Frank raped and murdered Mary Phagan and tried to blame the negro, Jim Conley; the workers testified against him. When the whites lynched Frank, the ADL was formed so that no so-called Jewish man would be convicted again, and they never reveal that they blamed a black man.
